revenue: Net sales rose 2.8% to $7,647mm on a 4.8% increase in average daily sales — higher volumes plus contributions from acquisitions — partially offset by one fewer selling week versus the 53-week FY2024. Growth was broad-based (PVF +2.6%, storm drainage +4.1%, meters +3.5%), with fire protection up only 0.7% and driven more by higher average selling prices than volume.
gross_profit: Gross margin expanded ~30bps to 26.9% from 26.6%, with gross profit up $79mm to $2,059mm. Management attributes the improvement to execution of its gross margin initiatives and disciplined purchasing and pricing management rather than to volume.
operating_income: Operating income was essentially flat at $722mm (+0.4%), so operating margin slipped to ~9.4% from ~9.7% as SG&A grew 7.1% — far faster than the 2.8% sales increase. The SG&A build reflects higher acquisition-related costs, higher personnel and variable compensation/benefits, and inflation-driven distribution expenses plus technology investment, only partly offset by the lost week and cost reduction initiatives; D&A was flat at $183mm as runoff on existing intangibles offset amortization from recent deals.
interest_expense: Interest expense fell $22mm to $120mm, helped by the FY2024 amendments that cut the effective applicable margin on the Senior Term Loan Credit Facility, lower benchmark rates, and reduced ABL borrowings (no ABL balance outstanding at year-end). Cash interest paid dropped even more sharply, from $197mm to $133mm.
pre_tax: Pre-tax income rose $30mm to $607mm (7.9% margin vs 7.8%), driven almost entirely by the lower interest burden plus $5mm of other income, since operating income was essentially flat. The effective tax rate also eased to 23.9% from 24.8% on tax credit investment benefits and equity award windfalls, lifting net income 6.5% to $462mm.
current_assets: Current assets grew to $2,302mm from $2,025mm against roughly flat current liabilities of $874mm, so the current ratio improved to ~2.6x. The swing is almost entirely cash, which jumped from $8mm to $220mm as acquisition spending fell $680mm year over year, with inventory also up $78mm and receivables slightly lower.
inventory: Inventories rose to $986mm from $908mm, reflecting a $70mm working capital build in operating cash flow and acquired inventory. Even so, the quick ratio improved because the $212mm cash build more than offset the inventory increase; note carrying value is net of supplier rebates, which grew to $64mm from $54mm.
total_debt: Total debt declined to $2,148mm from $2,261mm as the company repaid the $93mm net ABL drawdown and made $24mm of scheduled term loan amortization, with no new issuance in FY2025 (versus $950mm of term debt issued in FY2024 to fund acquisitions). The $493mm swing in net debt activity was the main driver of the shift to financing cash outflow.
ebitda: Standard EBITDA rose modestly to $913mm from $905mm, tracking the small increase in net income net of lower interest expense, with D&A flat at $186mm and taxes roughly unchanged. In substance, gross profit gains of $79mm were nearly fully consumed by the $76mm SG&A increase, so EBITDA growth lagged sales; combined with lower debt, leverage improves to roughly 2.4x from 2.5x.
operating_cash: Operating cash flow improved $29mm to $650mm on lower interest payments ($133mm vs $197mm cash paid), lower income tax payments ($79mm vs $143mm) and higher net income, partially offset by a heavier working capital investment — a $70mm inventory build and $59mm reduction in accounts payable, cushioned by a $26mm receivables release and $48mm increase in accrued liabilities.
